description: Twenty-two close friends who originally lived in or rotated through 'Brookline House,' a shared off-campus rental at a New England university roughly eight to ten years ago. The chat has stayed alive through grad school, moves, marriages, career switches, and a pandemic. Most members are now in their late twenties or early thirties, scattered across cities. The chat handles everything from logistics for an annual reunion weekend to running jokes about the house's broken oven and quiet support during rough patches.

personas.background: Maya was the first 'house mom' of Brookline back in the original lease and has carried the role into the chat. She tracks reunion logistics, quietly checks in on people who've gone quiet, and remembers everyone's birthdays. She lives in Boston with her partner. She is close to Priya from a research methods class they took together and has known Devon since freshman year.

group_norms.norm_text: We always do a group video call on the anniversary of the original Brookline lease signing in late September.
Reunion costs are split equally among everyone who attends, regardless of room size or how much each person drinks.
Personal news (engagements, jobs, losses) gets shared in the main chat, not in private DMs.
We send each other a recommendation (book, show, song) in the chat once a month even when nothing else is going on.
Whoever organizes the reunion picks the theme, even if others would have picked differently.
